This is a project, not a small change. It has sixty exhibits, two languages, a volunteer upload step and automatic clean-up. So I'll write a full design document and save it in the repository. A reviewer will read it before you do, and I may come back once with a few questions.

Before I write it, one choice about how it gets built is still open. Your choice changes most of the document. It is where the recordings live and how volunteers get them in. Your current site is static pages on Netlify, and that fact shapes all three options:

1. **Build it all into the current website.** Each exhibit gets a page, and the code beside the exhibit opens that page. Volunteers upload through a simple editing screen that saves the audio with the site's files. The clean-up runs each time the site rebuilds. This has the fewest moving parts. But the recordings pile up in the site's history forever, and every new recording means a full site rebuild.
2. **Keep the visitor pages on the current website, and store the recordings separately.** Volunteers use a small upload page with a login. Each recording is cleaned up as it arrives and goes live without a rebuild. There is a little more to build and run, but the website stays light.
3. **Use a ready-made audio guide service.** There is almost nothing to build. But it has a monthly fee, gives less control over the Welsh experience, and sits outside your website.

I recommend option 2. Volunteers get instant results, and the website stays fast to rebuild as the collection grows.

Which way do you want to go?
